texts.li: [theirFaith] Pilgrims of {PLACE} from {FACTION} are at the gate, dusty to the knees. They have walked a long way to pray before {TALE}, and they ask whether the doors of the reliquary might be opened to them for a day.\n\nThey would pray at the gate if that is all the colony allows.

[converts] A few of {FACTION}'s people have come to {PLACE}, though their own people haven't, and they walked here to pray before {TALE}. Their leader asks at the gate whether they may be let in to the reliquary for a day.\n\nThey have little, but they would leave something for the shrine if it were asked.
[believer] {A_nameDef} saw them first: pilgrims of {PLACE} at the gate, heads bowed, asking to pray before {TALE}. They came from {FACTION}, and they would like to go in to the reliquary itself.

li.label: Open the doors to the reliquary
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walked the pilgrims in, and they prayed before {TALE} through the day before going home.

li.label: Let them pray at the gate
li.outcome: The pilgrims prayed at the gate for a few hours, facing the reliquary, then went on.

li.label: Ask an offering for the shrine ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The pilgrims counted out {COUNT} silver at the gate and were let in to pray before {TALE}. A few of the colony's own faithful didn't like to see it asked.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: The pilgrims were told the reliquary is not for visitors, and went back the way they came.

texts.li: [tribal] Folk of {FACTION} are at the gate with bare feet and painted hands. They have heard the colony keeps an anima tree, and they ask to sit before it for a day and a night, as their elders taught them.\n\nWhere they meditate, they say, the tree's grass comes up thicker.

[empire] Psycasters of {FACTION} have stopped at the gate on their way through. Anima trees are rare, their leader says, and they would like to meditate at the colony's for a day. They would pay for the privilege, if the colony asked.

Travelers of {FACTION} who meditate at anima trees wherever they find them are at the gate. They ask leave to sit before the colony's tree for a day.\n\nThe tree's grass grows where people meditate before it, whoever they are.
[psycaster] Meditators of {FACTION} are at the gate, asking after the colony's anima tree. {A_nameDef}, who knows the tree's quiet as well as anyone, could sit with them.

li.label: Welcome them, and feed them
li.outcome: The pilgrims meditated in a ring before the anima tree from morning into the night, and {A_nameDef} spent a while with them there. Their meditation fed the tree's grass as a colonist's does.

li.label: sitting with the pilgrims at the tree
Let them in, for a fee ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The pilgrims paid {COUNT} silver at the gate and meditated at the tree for a few hours before going on.

li.label: Keep them away from the tree
li.outcome: The pilgrims were told the tree is the colony's own, and went on.

texts.li: [theirKind,skill] Folk of {FACTION} are at the gate, asking for {A_nameDef} by name. They are {TALE}, as {A_pronoun} is, and word reached them that one of their own blood lives here.\n\nThey would stay the night if asked, and they know a thing or two about {SKILL}.

[fewOfThem] There are not many of {A_nameDef}'s kind among {FACTION}, and the few {TALE} there heard that {A_pronoun} lives here. Now they are at the gate, asking for {A_objective} by name.\n\nThey would like an evening with one of their own.
Travelers of {FACTION} are at the gate, {TALE} like {A_nameDef}. They heard one of their own blood lives at the colony, and they would like to meet {A_objective}.

li.label: Host them for the night
li.outcome: {A_nameDef}'s kin stayed the night by the gate. {A_nameDef} spent the evening with them at the fire, and before they went they showed {A_objective} a thing or two of their own.

li.label: an evening at the fire with {A_nameDef}'s kin
A word with {A_nameDef} at the gate
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went out to the gate and talked with them a while. They went on before evening, glad to have met {A_objective}.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {A_nameDef}'s kin were told {A_pronoun} couldn't be spared. They looked toward the colony a long moment, and went.

texts.li: Half of {PLACE} saw {TALE} come down, and a few of them walked out to see it close. They are at the gate now, craning their necks at the hull, asking whether someone might show them round it.\n\nThey brought a few things of their own to trade, too.

Folk of {FACTION} from {PLACE} have walked out to the colony to see the ship that came down out of the sky. They would give a good deal to walk round {TALE}, they say, and they have goods with them if the colony would rather trade.

li.label: Show them round the hull
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walked the folk from {PLACE} round {TALE}, answering questions until the light went. They will talk about it in {PLACE} for a long time.

li.label: showing the gawkers round the ship
Trade at the gate ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The folk from {PLACE} set down their goods at the gate and took the colony's {COUNT} silver home, still looking back at the ship.

li.label: Keep them back from the ship
li.outcome: The folk from {PLACE} were kept at the gate. They looked at {TALE} from there a while, and walked home.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walks the roads with a pack of books and swaps them one for one. {X_pronoun} heard the colony has {TALE}, and offers {PLACE} for it.\n\nOr {X_pronoun} would pay {COUNT} silver, or sit a day at the colony's shelf and copy it out.

[theirsBetter] A reader from {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, is at the gate with a pack full of books. {X_pronoun} offers {PLACE}, a finer copy than most, for the colony's {TALE}.\n\nShort of a swap, {X_pronoun} would buy it for {COUNT} silver, or borrow it a day to copy.

[theirsWorse] {X_nameDef}, a reader from {FACTION}, would like {TALE}, and offers {PLACE} for it, though {X_possessive} copy has seen better days.\n\n{X_pronoun} would pay {COUNT} silver instead, or copy it at the colony's shelf if it can't be spared.

li.label: Swap them
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took {TALE} and left {PLACE} in its place.

li.label: Lend it for copying
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spent the day at the colony's bookcase, copying {TALE} into a notebook, and left the book where it was.

li.label: Sell it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took {TALE} and left {COUNT} silver in its place.

li.label: Keep the colony's books
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugged, shouldered the pack and went on to the next town.

texts.li: [friend] {X_nameDef} the {TALE} is back, and not alone: {X_pronoun} married {PLACE} on the road since the last visit. {X_pronoun} wanted {A_nameDef} to be the first here to know, and brought a carving for {A_objective}.

{X_nameDef}, the {TALE} the colony knows well, is at the gate with {PLACE}, married since the last time through. {X_pronoun} has brought a carving for {A_nameDef}, and a story about how it all happened.

li.label: A wedding gift (60 silver)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carried a purse of silver out to the gate for the new couple. {X_nameDef} said the colony would hear about the children, when there were any.

li.label: Wish them well at the gate
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went out to the gate to wish the couple well, and they went on before evening.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {PLACE} were sent on their way.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} the {TALE} is back, with a child at {X_possessive} side: {PLACE}, found alone on the road and kept ever since. {X_pronoun} brought a carving for {A_nameDef} too.
[friend] {X_nameDef} is at the gate with {PLACE}, a child {X_pronoun} took in on the road. {X_pronoun} wanted {A_nameDef} to meet the child, and brought a carving for {A_objective}.

li.label: A warm coat for the child
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} brought out a coat from the colony's stores for {PLACE} to take on the road.

li.label: An evening at the fire
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {PLACE} stayed the night, and spent the evening at the colony's fire with {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {PLACE} were sent on their way.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} the {TALE} is back, slower than before, with a young one at {X_possessive} side: {PLACE}, the apprentice who will walk the road in {X_possessive} place. This is {X_possessive} last time round, {X_pronoun} says. {X_pronoun} brought a carving for {A_nameDef}, to remember {X_objective} by.

[friend] {X_nameDef} wanted {A_nameDef} to meet {PLACE}, the apprentice who will carry the trade on. The knees won't take the road much longer, {X_pronoun} says, and there is a carving for {A_nameDef} in {X_possessive} pack.

li.label: Take {PLACE} on as the colony's {TALE}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went out to the gate to meet {PLACE}. From now on it is {PLACE} the colony will see coming up the road.

li.label: A last lesson from {X_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent a while at {X_nameDef}'s side, learning one last thing of the trade, and then the two travelers went on.

li.label: Thank them at the gate
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} thanked {X_nameDef} at the gate for all the years, and {X_nameDef} and {PLACE} went on down the road together.

texts.li: [old] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is at the gate with word of {DEAD} the {TALE}: {DEAD} died on the road, of nothing but old age, in a bed {X_pronoun} had found for the night. {DEAD} asked that a carving be brought to {A_nameDef}, and {X_nameDef} has brought it.

[ill] {X_nameDef}, who walked the road with {DEAD} the {TALE}, is at the gate. {DEAD} died of {RELATION} a few weeks back, {X_pronoun} says, and wanted {A_nameDef} to have the carving in {X_possessive} pack.

li.label: Keep a vigil for {DEAD}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and a few others kept watch at the gate that night for {DEAD}, as the colony does for its own.

li.label: Send silver for those {DEAD} left (50 silver)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carried silver out to {X_nameDef} for {DEAD}'s people, and {X_nameDef} promised to see it into the right hands.

li.label: Thank {X_nameDef} for the word
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} was thanked for the word, and went on.
